QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_47

question.text: In early-stage / pre-revenue startup valuation, a commonly cited qualitative score-card framework assigns value across five factors. Which of the following sets of factors aligns with this qualitative approach?

answer.text: Qualitative score-card across five factors: sound idea, prototype, quality management team, strategic relationships, and product rollout/sales

explanation.text: The Logic: The five-factor qualitative score-card (sometimes attributed to the Berkus method in PE/VC practice) is commonly applied to pre-revenue startups where standard valuation methods (DCF, P/E, comparables) are unreliable. It assigns value across non-financial drivers — quality of the idea, working prototype, management team, strategic partnerships, and the product/sales rollout. The Trap: Revenue-only, P/E-only, and asset-only valuation approaches do not capture the dominant non-financial drivers of early-stage value. Note: The XIX-A workbook covers qualitative valuation judgement, IPEV method-selection factors, and startup qualitative score-card attributes generally, but does not specifically name the Berkus method or its exact factor list. Treat this as general VC industry knowledge applicable when reading IPEV-guided valuation policies.
